summary: A worker brought in through a current employee stays longer than someone who applied cold, which is why the employer values the favor.
realLife: Researchers studying call centers and trucking found referred hires were much less likely to quit and cost less to recruit than nonreferred hires.
sources: University of Minnesota research profile, The value of hiring through employee referrals (Quarterly Journal of Economics): https://experts.umn.edu/en/publications/the-value-of-hiring-through-employee-referrals/
inGame: new-coworker event with a tie to the referrer; later job-ended events by quitting can be compared.

turns.summary: The new hire settles in and the referrer's standing rises.
turns.writesBack: referrer tie closer; boss thinks well of referrer

turns.summary: The hire does poorly and the referrer is embarrassed.
turns.writesBack: referrer tie colder; boss trust lower

turns.summary: Both quit within a year for another firm.
turns.writesBack: two job-ended events; employer loses both
